A1.justification: Both PDFs describe STaR-Bets and contain readable main text, equations, algorithms, figures, and Appendices A-D. Reformatting and pagination changes do not prevent reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original Bernoulli and Beta simulations measuring interval widths and empirical coverage, including 1,000-repetition comparisons and ablations in Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 retains these original simulation results in Figures 1-3 and Appendix C. Results retained from v1 remain original empirical contributions.

M1.justification: The betting procedures in Algorithms 1-6 and the implementation modifications in Appendix D remain unchanged. Bets already appeared as Algorithm 3 and in the ablations; its increased prominence does not introduce a new method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate bounded-mean estimation using the same Bernoulli and Beta distribution families and scenarios. The new confidence-sequence discussion is theoretical and introduces no evaluated task.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain Hedged-CI, T-test, PMBSS, Hoeffding, empirical Bernstein, and standard/randomized Clopper-Pearson where applicable. The newly cited Shekhar-Ramdas work is not added as an experimental comparator.

E3.justification: Figure 1's caption changes the reported candidate mean from m=0.85 to m=0.86, matching the plot title already present in v1. This corrects a documented setting without establishing a rerun. Other sample sizes, distribution parameters, metrics, and evaluation procedures are retained.

E4.justification: Appendix C retains the same analyses of delta sensitivity, estimator parameter c, final-round randomization, the STaR component, and sample-order shuffling. Their plots and substantive findings are unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions report 1,000 repetitions, empirical CDFs, and 0.95 one-sided confidence bounds for assessing coverage. No repeated-run counts, seed disclosures, or uncertainty-reporting procedures are added or revised.

E6.justification: Figures 2-3 and all Appendix C plots retain the same results, and Figure 1 preserves its plotted trajectories. Width comparisons, coverage findings, and ablation conclusions remain unchanged; Figure 1's corrections concern its axis labels and documented setting.

T1.justification: Theorem 8 adds the claim n0=O(c^-4), supported by additional constant-tracking assertions in Appendix A. Section 5 adds a confidence-sequence coverage argument and width bound. There are also local corrections to coin-betting arithmetic, the supermartingale expectation inequality, and optimization formulations. Removing the duplicated logarithm lemma loses no distinct result.

C1.justification: v1's introduction attributes provable optimality to STaR-Bets itself. v2 assigns the optimal-width guarantee to Bets while describing STaR-Bets through validity and empirical performance. This substantially narrows a central guarantee attached to the proposed algorithm, although the abstract remains broadly worded.

C2.justification: Section 5 explicitly acknowledges that the optimality properties proved separately do not establish optimality for their combination in Algorithm 4. It also explains the confidence-sequence interpretation and recommends other methods for that purpose. Existing empirical interpretations and implementation caveats are retained.

D1.justification: Section 4 explicitly confirms adoption of grid discretization, clarifying which previously described construction is used. Appendix D's clipping, final-round randomization, c=1 estimator choice, and the code-access link remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds Shekhar and Ramdas, 'On the near-optimality of betting confidence sets for bounded means,' and attributes the almost-sure asymptotic optimality result to them instead of Waudby-Smith and Ramdas. The broader related-work discussion remains stable.

P1.justification: v2 makes distributed grammar and terminology corrections, revises the experimental introduction, updates affiliation and conference information, and removes a duplicated appendix lemma. The section sequence and most explanatory prose remain intact.

P2.justification: Conference-template formatting changes fonts, margins, spacing, and figure placement. Figure 1 becomes rasterized, corrects candidate-mean ticks from 820-900 to 0.82-0.90, and aligns its caption with m=0.86. The remaining figures retain their panels and graphical content.

improvement.justification: v2 improves claim precision by separating Bets' theoretical guarantee from STaR-Bets' empirical superiority, and corrects attribution and figure labels. However, the new n0=O(c^-4) claim has an unresolved support problem: Appendix A asserts an O(n^-1/4) remainder while its displayed warm-up bound contains sqrt(c2), yielding n^-1/8 for the stated n^-1/4 choice of c2. This stronger guarantee is not established by the displayed tracking. The clearer limitations and newly questionable quantitative claim leave the net quality change uncertain.
